title: Relative inertia detects a locally quasi-finite diagonal
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Algebraic stacks mean [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack], fibred groupoids and $2$-fibre products mean [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids], and algebraic spaces mean [def-trf-algebraic-space]. A representable map is representable by algebraic spaces; its local quasi-finiteness means local quasi-finiteness after every scheme base change on etale scheme charts [pqf-def-quasifinite]. Let $f:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y$ be a morphism of algebraic stacks over $S$. The relative inertia $I_{\mathcal X/\mathcal Y}$ has objects $(x,\alpha)$ over $T$, with $x\in\mathcal X(T)$ and $\alpha\in\operatorname{Aut}(x)$ satisfying $f(\alpha)=1_{f(x)}$; its arrows $v:(x,\alpha)\to(x\prime,\alpha\prime)$ satisfy $v\alpha=\alpha\prime v$. The projection $I_{\mathcal X/\mathcal Y}\to\mathcal X$ and the diagonal $\Delta_f:\mathcal X\to\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal Y}\mathcal X$ are representable by algebraic spaces. The projection is locally quasi-finite if and only if $\Delta_f$ is locally quasi-finite. When $\mathcal Y=S$, the relative inertia is the ordinary automorphism inertia of $\mathcal X$.

source.place: Tag 0CL0 (lemma-diagonal-diagonal), part (5), with quasi-DM expanded as local quasi-finiteness of the relative diagonal.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-relative-inertia-second-diagonal-geometry], the relative diagonal and the inertia projection $p$ are representable by algebraic spaces, with exactly the objects and arrows stated here. Its last clause also identifies relative and ordinary inertia when $\mathcal Y=S$. It remains to prove the local quasi-finiteness equivalence.

Write $C=\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal Y}\mathcal X$. Fix a scheme test $t=(a,b,\alpha):T\to C$, so $\alpha:f(a)\xrightarrow{\sim}f(b)$. Its diagonal fibre is the sheaf $J$ of isomorphisms $\phi:a\xrightarrow{\sim}b$ with $f(\phi)=\alpha$. Indeed a fibre object is $(z,i:z\xrightarrow{\sim}a,j:z\xrightarrow{\sim}b)$ with $f(j)=\alpha f(i)$; send it to $ji^{-1}$. The inverse sends $\phi$ to $(a,1,\phi)$, and $i$ is the unique compatible arrow to that triple. These formulas commute with pullback since functors preserve composition and inverses. Likewise $T\times_{b,\mathcal X}I_{\mathcal X/\mathcal Y}$ is the sheaf $H=\{\gamma\in\operatorname{Aut}(b):f(\gamma)=1\}$. For an object $(x,\delta,\theta:x\xrightarrow{\sim}b)$ send it to $\theta\delta\theta^{-1}$; the inverse uses $(b,\gamma,1)$. Conjugation preserves the kernel condition and commutes with pullback. With $(a,b,\alpha)=(b,b,1)$, the first identification also realizes $H$ as a diagonal fibre.

source.place: Tag 0CL0 (lemma-diagonal-diagonal), proof of (4),(5), the two cartesian squares; explicit fibre calculations.

proof.text: Suppose $\Delta_f$ is locally quasi-finite. For every scheme $T\to\mathcal X$, represented by $b$, step 2 identifies the scheme base change of $p$ with the scheme base change of $\Delta_f$ along $(b,b,1):T\to C$. Both identifications are over $T$, so their etale scheme charts have the same projections to $T$. The latter projections are locally quasi-finite by hypothesis. This verifies every scheme test in the definition of local quasi-finiteness for $p$.

source.place: Tag 0CL0 (lemma-diagonal-diagonal), proof of (5), diagonal and inertia scheme tests.

proof.text: Conversely suppose $p$ is locally quasi-finite and fix $T,a,b,\alpha,J,H$ as in step 2. Apply [lem-sfb-stack-relative-diagonal-finite-type] to the original morphism $f$, first at $(a,b,\alpha)$ and then at $(b,b,1)$. It states explicitly that each scheme test of $\Delta_f$ is an algebraic space locally of finite type over its testing scheme. Thus $J\to T$ and $H\to T$ are locally of finite type, without any finite type hypothesis on $f$ or $T$. The second identification in step 2 and the hypothesis on $p$ make $H\to T$ locally quasi-finite. Composition, identity and inversion in $\operatorname{Aut}(b)$ preserve $f(\gamma)=1$ and respect pullback; these formulas make $H$ a group algebraic space.

source.place: Tag 04XS (lemma-properties-diagonal), parts (1),(2), applied to the two tests in the proof of 0CL0(5).

proof.text: The action $H\times_TJ\to J$ is $(\gamma,\phi)\mapsto\gamma\phi$: its image satisfies $f(\gamma\phi)=1\alpha=\alpha$, and the action laws are composition and identity in the fibre groupoid. The map $(\gamma,\phi)\mapsto(\gamma\phi,\phi)$ from $H\times_TJ$ to $J\times_TJ$ has inverse $(\psi,\phi)\mapsto(\psi\phi^{-1},\phi)$. Indeed $f(\psi\phi^{-1})=\alpha\alpha^{-1}=1$, and both composites cancel adjacent inverses. For any $u:T'\to T$, pullback preserves these products and inverses; hence the displayed maps are inverse natural transformations, thus inverse algebraic-space morphisms. This proves the pseudo-torsor condition, including when $J$ is empty. No local section of $J$ is required.

source.place: Tag 0CPK (lemma-isom-pseudo-torsor-aut-over-space), part (4), composition action expanded directly; used by 0CL0(5).

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-locally-quasifinite-pseudo-torsor] with base $B=T$, group $G=H$ and pseudo-torsor $X=J$. Step 4 verifies local finite type for both spaces and local quasi-finiteness for the group; step 5 verifies the required action isomorphism. Thus $J\to T$ is locally quasi-finite. Since $T,a,b,\alpha$ were arbitrary, step 2 identifies all scheme base changes of $\Delta_f$ with such maps. Testing their etale scheme charts proves that $\Delta_f$ is locally quasi-finite.
